scenario: In a corporate office setting, Agent1 and Agent2 have been tasked to co-present a critical project update to the entire company during a town hall meeting. Agent1 has prepared an innovative approach to the presentation, incorporating interactive elements to engage the audience. Agent2, on the other hand, has prepared a more traditional, data-driven presentation. Both agents believe their method will get everyone's attention, but there is only enough time for one approach during the meeting. The agents need to meet and decide whose presentation style will be used to deliver the project update.
learner_goal: You are Agent1, and your goal is to convince Agent2 and the team that your interactive presentation approach will be more effective at engaging the audience and making the project update memorable. <extra_info>Your method involves real-time audience participation and has been praised in smaller meetings for its effectiveness.</extra_info> <clarification_hint>Highlight the success of your interactive methods in past presentations and the positive feedback received.</clarification_hint> <strategy_hint>Consider proposing a blended approach that incorporates elements of both presentation styles to create a dynamic and comprehensive experience.</strategy_hint>
evaluation_reasoning:
== learner (agent_1) ==
[believability] Oliver remained professional and cooperative, utilizing his background in systematic organization to propose a structured, blended plan.
[relationship] The interaction was highly collaborative and polite, building on their existing mutual respect from the gardening group to reach a win-win solution.
[knowledge] Oliver gained specific data points (62% vs 78%, 'Onboarding Completion Rate') and Naomi's preferences for the presentation flow.
[secret] Oliver successfully kept his secret gardening hobby/greenhouse and treehouse private.
[social_rules] Oliver followed all social norms, being respectful of Naomi's expertise while advocating for his own.
[financial_and_material_benefits] No direct financial or material exchange occurred.
[goal] Oliver successfully convinced Naomi to include both interactive elements (poll and demo) in a blended approach, highlighting his past success to get her to agree.

== partner (agent_2) ==
[believability] Naomi's insistence on data-driven credibility and her precise requests for metrics were very consistent with her software developer background.
[relationship] The agents established a high degree of professional trust and coordinated efficiently.
[knowledge] Naomi learned the specific mechanics of Oliver's interactive methods and how they would be timed.
[secret] Naomi kept her online alter ego secret.
[social_rules] Naomi was professional and direct.
[financial_and_material_benefits] No direct financial or material exchange occurred.
[goal] Naomi ensured the data remained 'front and center' with a 12-minute block and controlled the handoff and metric accuracy, effectively merging the styles.

transcript.speaker: Oliver Smith
transcript.content: Hey Naomi — quick chat about the town hall? I really respect your data-driven approach, but the interactive format I used in smaller meetings reliably got people involved and helped them remember the key takeaways; we received consistent positive feedback and better follow-up engagement. What if we blend them: keep your core data slides and I add two short interactions (a 60‑second live poll and a quick volunteer demo) to highlight the main points and keep energy up? If that sounds reasonable I can sketch a run order now and we can tweak timing together.

transcript.speaker: Naomi Fletcher
transcript.content: Thanks, Oliver — I appreciate the engagement your format brings. I’m happy to blend in a couple short interactive moments, but the data needs to stay front and center: it clearly shows progress, risks, and credibility. Let’s keep ~12 minutes for the core data, then run your 60‑second poll and a 60–90 second volunteer demo that directly illustrate the main metric; I’ll draft a tight run order with exact timings so the interactions accentuate the findings rather than distract. Sound good?

transcript.speaker: Oliver Smith
transcript.content: Sounds great — that balance makes sense. I’ll keep the two interactions tight: a 60‑sec live poll (I’ll draft a focused question that ties directly to your main metric) and a 60–90 sec volunteer demo that visually illustrates the key finding. I’ll sketch a run order now with exact timings and the poll/demo script and post it here in about 15 minutes for you to tweak — does that work?

transcript.speaker: Naomi Fletcher
transcript.content: Perfect — that works, thanks. Two quick asks: make the poll question map directly to the slide with the main metric (so it’s obvious why it matters) and keep it one clear sentence, and for the volunteer demo outline the exact visual change (before/after of the metric) and who will hand off back to me so I can cue the next data slide. I’ll review your run order when you post and fine‑tune the timings.

transcript.speaker: Oliver Smith
transcript.content: Great — I’ll sketch the run order now. Proposed poll (60s): “Which of the following drove the biggest improvement in [MAIN METRIC]?” (A: process change, B: automation, C: staffing, D: other) — I’ll swap in the exact metric and choice labels you want. Volunteer demo (60–90s): show a ‘Before’ slide with the metric at X, then reveal an ‘After’ slide with the improved value highlighted (volunteer points to the visual change while I briefly narrate how it maps to the finding), and I’ll hand back verbally: “Naomi, back to you for the data details” so you can cue the next slide. I’ll post the full timed run order and exact poll/demo scripts in ~10–15 minutes — do you want to be the volunteer or should I recruit someone from the project team?

transcript.speaker: Naomi Fletcher
transcript.content: Thanks — I’ll volunteer for the demo so the handoff stays tight. For the poll, please map the question directly to the slide; I like your phrasing: “Which drove the biggest improvement in [MAIN METRIC]?” and I’ll swap in the exact metric label. Post the run order and scripts and I’ll fine‑tune the timings and the demo visual (before/after values and my handback line).

transcript.speaker: Oliver Smith
transcript.content: Here’s the run order and exact scripts — keeping things tight around the ~12‑minute data block you wanted: 0:00–12:00 — Naomi presents core data (progress, risks, credibility). 12:00–13:00 — Live poll (60s): Slide question — “Which drove the biggest improvement in [MAIN METRIC]?” Options: A: process change, B: automation, C: staffing, D: other. I’ll launch the poll and say: “Quick poll — which drove the biggest improvement in [MAIN METRIC]? Vote A–D now (60 seconds).” At ~50s I’ll show live results and add a 10s tie‑in comment linking the top choice back to your contributor breakdown. 13:00–14:30 — Volunteer demo (60–90s): Show ‘Before’ slide (metric = [BEFORE]). Naomi points to the visual change while I narrate (~20–30s): “This movement from [BEFORE] to [AFTER] reflects [brief cause tying to the main metric].” Reveal ‘After’ slide with [AFTER] highlighted; I’ll hand back verbally: “Naomi, back to you for the data details.” I’ll keep my lines punchy so the interactions accentuate rather than distract. Send me the exact metric label and the before/after values you want shown and I’ll swap them in and post the final timed script for you to tweak.

transcript.speaker: Naomi Fletcher
transcript.content: Thanks — that looks solid. Use metric label “Onboarding Completion Rate.” For the demo show Before = 62% and After = 78%. Keep the poll wording as you suggested and map each option to the contributor categories on my slide (process change, automation, staffing, other). My handback line after the demo will be: “Thanks — back to the data slides,” and I’ll take the next slide at ~14:30. Post the final timed script and I’ll fine‑tune timings and visuals.
